deltas.before: update calls mergeAssetGovernance, which only fills empty inputs and therefore permits any non-empty observation payload to overwrite governance fields
deltas.after: branch on the two approved ActionID values before assigning the next record; observation update preserves every governance field and stale observation preserves every observation field
exact_code_actions: reject an ActionID outside asset-upsert and asset-observation-upsert before the first authority write
for asset-upsert keep expected-revision CAS and apply the manual rows of ASSET-UPsert-SOURCE-PRECEDENCE-V1
for asset-observation-upsert copy governance fields from existing and copy observation fields only when observedAt is not older than existing.LastSeen
derive create defaults from the approved contract instead of trusting observation-supplied governance values
do not add a polymorphic Command abstraction; the selected design remains a direct transaction coordinator
deltas.compatibility: preserve the exported method signature and existing manual action semantics; the behavior change is intentionally fail-closed for observation governance writes
deltas.rollback: restore the prior branch only before rollout; after a committed bad observation use a new expected-revision forward fix and retain history and audit

deltas.before: jsonObject in postgres.go converts Tags or Metadata marshal failure into an empty object, so UpsertAtomic cannot distinguish corrupt input from an intentional empty object
deltas.after: UpsertAtomic serializes Tags and Metadata into checked local byte slices before INSERT or UPDATE and returns ERR-ASSET-WRITE without executing the authority statement when either serialization fails
exact_code_actions: call json.Marshal for rec.Tags and rec.Metadata after B08 and before the branch SQL
bind the checked byte slices to both INSERT and UPDATE parameters instead of invoking jsonObject
wrap each error with a stable internal stage without placing payload or tenant identity in the public message
deltas.compatibility: the stored JSON representation remains an object and the SQL column contract is unchanged
deltas.rollback: no database effect exists before serialization succeeds; code rollback restores the old encoder without deleting committed rows

deltas.before: oldJSON, _ = json.Marshal(existing) discards the encoder error and can commit an update with an inaccurate nullable old_value
deltas.after: capture the error from json.Marshal(existing), return ERR-HISTORY-MARSHAL and let deferred rollback remove the staged authority update
exact_code_actions: replace the blank identifier with oldJSON, err = json.Marshal(existing)
return a wrapped stable history-encode error immediately when err is non-nil
retain the existing checked new-state marshal and ensure neither path reaches asset_events on failure
deltas.compatibility: successful history JSON bytes remain unchanged; only previously silent invariant violations become explicit rollback
deltas.rollback: deferred transaction rollback is the only data action; no compensating delete is allowed

deltas.before: auditDetail, _ = json.Marshal(...) discards an audit encoder error and may insert an incomplete detail value
deltas.after: capture the audit serialization error, return a stable audit-encode error and rollback authority, history and audit staging before outbox construction
exact_code_actions: add ERR-AUDIT-MARSHAL to the function error algebra
replace the blank identifier with auditDetail, err := json.Marshal(...) and check err before ExecContext
add a fault test whose oracle reconciles zero rows across all five included effects
deltas.compatibility: successful audit JSON bytes and audit table columns remain unchanged
deltas.rollback: return before the audit INSERT and rely on the transaction rollback; never delete immutable audit after commit

deltas.before: both replay commit and new-write commit return fmt-wrapped generic errors; HTTP maps generic errors to 400 with err.Error and gRPC maps them to Internal with err.Error
deltas.after: repository returns a typed commit-unknown sentinel carrying stage but no secret; HTTP and gRPC leaves map it to an unknown/pending receipt-recovery response and require the original tenant, idempotency key and payload hash
exact_code_actions: declare ErrAssetCommitUnknown in atomic_upsert.go and wrap both tx.Commit error sites with errors.Is support
do not retry inside UpsertAtomic and do not generate a new idempotency key
in the independent HTTP leaf return a stable operation-unknown code and safe message without err.Error
in the independent gRPC leaf return Unavailable or an approved operation-unknown status without err.Error
the independent PostgreSQL TST-PRE leaf injects response loss and proves same-key convergence to one stored receipt
deltas.compatibility: revision and idempotency conflicts retain their existing stable conflict mappings; only ambiguous commit stops being misreported as definitive failure
deltas.rollback: after an ambiguous commit query the original receipt; never issue a new intent or delete a possibly committed effect

non_goals: this delta does not modify Kafka publication or mark an outbox row published
this delta does not introduce per-field provenance storage or a migration
this delta does not claim its planned tests have run or that the WRT leaf is executable
blockers: HTTP, gRPC, test and real-broker changes require their own registered atomic leaves
